question.leadin: Answer the following about the Edo period.
question.text: During the Edo period, Japan was ruled by this family, for whom the period is also sometimes named. Ieyasu (EE-ay-ah-soo), a member of this family, won the Battle of Sekigahara to begin the Edo period.
question.clue: This Japanese clan the ruled from Edo. This clan headed the last feudal military government of Japan, and their first shogun was Ieyasu.

swap.text: This Japanese admiral commanded the pilots at Pearl Harbor. His plane was shot down on Bougainville Island during Operation Vengeance in 1943.
swap.answerHtml: Isoroku Yamamoto [or Yamamoto Isoroku, since Japanese names are traditionally written in reverse order]
swap.clue: During the reign of Hirohito, this naval leader was opposed to signing the Tripartite Pact. However, he still orchestrated the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor.

question.text: The battle for this island, home to three Japanese air fields, saw the raising of an American flag on top of its Mount Suribachi.
question.clue: Mass casualties were inflicted on marines during this battle by troops with flamethrowers in a tunnel system that had gone undetected.

swap.leadin: Give the following about surprise attacks in Japanese history.
swap.text: In the 1560 Battle of Okehazama, this daimyo's forces sneaked to the rear of the opposing army, killing the opposing leader at his tent. This unifier of Japan was succeeded by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu.
swap.clue: This man was forced to commit seppuku after being betrayed by Akechi Mitsuhide at Honno-ji.

question.text: This document officially ceded power to Emperor Meiji whose third clause allowed the ability to pursue any occupation regardless of social standing.
question.clue: This document was created when Emperor Meiji took power in 1868. It laid out Meiji's goals for Westernization, and can be considered the first constitution of modern-day Japan.

swap.leadin: These people were required to travel between two residences under the Sankin Kotai system.
swap.text: Give this term for a powerful landholding Japanese military lord under the Ashikaga. Their power was severely decreased during the reign of Tokugawa Ieyasu.
swap.clue: During the Edo period, they controlled three-fourths of the land not held by the bakufu, and under Tokugawa rule, they came to be known as kinsei, or "early modern."

question.leadin: Because of the 1955 System, this party has continually kept power in their country.
question.text: Name this political party, whose leader, Shinzo Abe ("AH-bay"), was assassinated in 2022. After the assassination, this party cut ties with the Unification Church.
question.answerHtml: Liberal Democratic Party [or LDP or Lib Dem or Jiyū-Minshutō or Jimintō reject “Liberal” or “Democratic” alone]
question.clue: This right-wing party which has traditionally dominated the Diet since the end of World War Two.

swap.leadin: Their duty is to "grasp the long and the short swords and to die."
swap.text: Name this bushido-obeying warrior class of feudal Japan.
swap.clue: Members of this group could find a job by embarking on a type of pilgrimage called musha shugyo, and their only goal should be "to grasp the long and the short swords and to die".

question.leadin: Answer the following about the period after the disintegration of the Ashikaga Shogunate.
question.text: The Shogunate collapsed during the Onin war between the clans Hosokawa and Yamana, marking the beginning of this period. This period included the overthrow of Ashikaga Yoshiaki by Oda Nobunaga following his conquest of Kyoto.
question.clue: First, name this Japanese historical period in which central power was weaker than under the shogunates.

swap.text: Yoshitsune's victories over the Taira clan enabled Minamoto Yoritomo to begin the Kamakura period by becoming the first man to claim this title, the military ruler of Japan.
swap.clue: Ishida Mitsunari was defeated by a prominent holder of this title at the Battle of Sekigahara.

question.leadin: This work's title character marries Lady Aoi before fathering his only child with Akashi's daughter.
question.text: Name this Heian period work, sometimes called the world's first novel, written by Lady Murasaki.
question.clue: This work, often called the world's first novel, is an important insight into Heian court life. It features the blank chapter "Vanished into the Clouds" and was written by Lady Murasaki Shikibu.

swap.text: Admirals Togo and Rozhestvensky faced off in this pivotal naval victory for Japan in the Russo-Japanese War, which was fought in the narrows between the Korean peninsula and Honshu.
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Tsushima Strait/s [or Tsusimskoye srazheniye; prompt on Battle of the Sea of Japan]
swap.clue: At the end of this battle, Admiral Nebogatov surrendered rather than doom his 2,000-plus sailors; regardless, his fleet had lost six battleships and twenty-eight other ships in a single day after eight months of sailing from the Baltic Sea.

question.leadin: Name these dudes from Asian history who founded dynasties.
question.text: After the Taira clan was defeated in the Battle of Dannoura, ending the Genpei War, this man became the first shogun of the Kamakura dynasty.
question.clue: This man seduced the daughter of his warden after he was banished to Izu for twenty years when his father tried to remove Taira Kiyomori in the Heiji Disturbance.

swap.text: The post-World War II Japanese constitution contained this article, which renounced the national right to war and use of force in international disputes. Despite this article, Japan maintains self-defense forces that serve as a de facto military.

question.text: This period, in which Suiko ("soo-ee-ko") and Shotoku ruled, saw several notable Korean monks such as Illa and Hyepyeon ("h'YEH-pyun") establish themselves in Japan. This period lies between the Kofun and Nara periods.
question.clue: Prince Shotoku proclaimed the Confucian 17 Article Constitution during this period, part of a series of moves to adopt Chinese customs.

swap.leadin: These laws brought about the development of estates called shoen.
swap.text: Name this set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.
swap.clue: The Asuka period ended with this set of reforms promulgated by the Kotoku Emperor which centralized power and introduced reorganization based on Tang Chinese lines.

question.leadin: Identify these leaders of 20th century Japan.
question.text: This man served as Emperor of Japan from 1912 to 1926. His reign is considered a golden age of Japanese democracy.
question.clue: This ruler, who ceded regency power to his son due to psychological problems. His country sent a list of twenty-one demands to a neighbor.

swap.text: Rusk told Yang that the maritime Macarthur Line would hold until this 1951 treaty took effect. This treaty names the US's "system" of "hub and spokes" bilateral defense treaties with Pacific countries, especially Japan.
swap.answerHtml: Treaty of San Francisco [or San Furanshisuko kōwa-Jōyaku; prompt on Treaty of Peace with Japan or U.S.-Japan Security Treaty (or Japanese equivalents) with “In what city was that treaty signed?]

question.text: The foremost predecessor of the LDP was the Liberal Party, which was led by this towering figure of post-WWII Japanese politics. He served as Prime Minister five times between 1946 and 1954, and formulated a namesake Doctrine for Japan's postwar recovery.

swap.leadin: The victorious force in this battle constructed wooden stockades to protect its valuable stock of Portuguese arquebusiers. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this 1575 battle which saw Takeda Katsuyori launch an unsuccessful siege of a certain castle on the Shitaragahara plain. In the first Samurai Warriors game, the defender Matsudaira Koretada is joined here by his resurrected father, Takeda Shingen.
swap.clue: Fearing a repeat of the events of Mikatagahara, one side's commander built a series of zigzagging wooden stockades and deployed his arquebusiers behind them.
